pullRequest.title: Clarify cloud-init example scope and Imager boundary
pullRequest.body:
### Summary

Clarify the scope of the existing `contrib/src/cloud-init` example.

The sample demonstrates NoCloud using separate `CIDATA` media. It does not provide general Raspberry Pi Imager customisation support.

Also clarify that rpi-image-gen's generated `image.json` is an Image Description Provisioning (IDP) document, not a Raspberry Pi Imager customisation manifest.

This should make the boundary between image generation, IDP provisioning, cloud-init, and Imager clearer.

Refs #182
Refs #184

nodes.body:
@kvnloo Thank your for pointing this out. As you noticed the contribution was not intended to be full-on network based cloud-init (and neither, for that matter is pi-gen's cloud-init configuration - that is aimed specifically at allowing things like Imager customisation), nor a Imager customisation manifest handler (in my view that belongs more with the [pi-gen](https://github.com/RPi-Distro/pi-gen), although this contribution could be used as a basis for understanding what is need to achieve either of those with rpi-image-gen.

I would like to propose something like the following instead of your text, which seems a little negative / 'glass half-empty' to me.

## Scope

This contribution is a NoCloud example, meant to allow firstboot customization for images that are
based on minimal image rather than modifying an full 'offical' PiOS image (for that the pi-gen repo 
is more suitable, at present).
 
The example expects cloud-init seed data from separate `CIDATA` media as
described below.

Neither this contribution, nor pi-gen's cloud-init support are full-on cloud-based cloud-init
configurations. In both cases further work is required, if that is what you seek.

The `image.json` generated by rpi-image-gen is an Image Description
Provisioning (IDP) document used by Raspberry Pi provisioning tooling. It is
not a Raspberry Pi Imager customisation manifest, and it is not intended to make it
Imager customisation capable.

An image must contain and enable a suitable integration for Imager-provided customisation
data to take effect. Currently the Image customisation is based on a modified cloud-init
configuration.

See the project provisioning documentation for the IDP format and scope
